gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Galaxy Tab Active5 Pro's 1.8 m drop rating counts only with its case on and that its screen is rated at 600 nits, which is below the 800–1,000-nit outdoor bar ChatGPT set itself. None states that the $3,498 Dell Pro Rugged 12 is rated for a 4 ft drop, against 6 ft for the Toughbook G2 and Getac UX10, or that the G2's '15 hours' needs the optional 68 Wh battery.
standout_why: Compared against the two cited Panasonic pages (connect.na.panasonic.com G2 and eu.connect.panasonic.com/ch G2) and the top roundups, itechguides.com and getac.com UX10; rottenwifi.com returned HTTP 502. The cited Panasonic EU page does give the 11 h standard and 15 h extended battery split, so that part is already covered. The cited US page states only '15 hours'. No result gives Samsung's brightness, says Samsung's drop rating needs the case, or gives a drop height for the Dell Pro Rugged 12. itechguides covers the older Latitude 7230 and has no Samsung or Panasonic drop or brightness figures. The rival pages do not put drop, brightness and battery side by side on one basis.
decides: ChatGPT made the Tab Active5 Pro its 'best value' pick and in the same answer told shoppers to look for 800–1,000+ nits. Samsung rates the screen at 600 nits, so for sunlit outdoor work the cheapest Android pick fails ChatGPT's own test, and Samsung's 1.8 m drop figure counts only with the case on. Among Windows tablets, the 'premium' Dell Pro Rugged 12 has the brightest screen (1,200 nits rated) and the largest standard battery (71.2 Wh, hot-swappable). Reviewers report a 4 ft drop, while Panasonic states 6 ft to plywood for the G2 and Getac states 6 ft while operating for the UX10. Drop-prone work such as utilities or ladders favours the G2 or UX10. Sun-heavy work with long shifts favours the Dell.

findings.note: Footnote: 'Tested on plywood (26 drops) MIL-STD 810H Method 516.8 Procedure IV', by an independent third-party lab. The US page reads '6' to plywood (3' with keyboard)'.

findings.label: Battery capacity vs MobileMark 25 runtime
findings.value: Standard 50 Wh ≈ 11 h; extended or quick-release 68 Wh ≈ 15 h
findings.note: Standard battery 11.4 V 4,360 mAh (50 Wh), extended 10.8 V 6,300 mAh (68 Wh). The cited US page (connect.na.panasonic.com) states only '15 hours - Mobile Mark 2025', which is the extended-battery figure.

findings.label: Brightness / IP / operating temp
findings.value: Up to 1,000 cd/m²; IP65 (digitiser listed IP55); −29 to 63 °C
findings.note: The full spec list gives 'IP55 Digitiser' separately from the IP65 headline and does not explain the difference. Hot-swap is optional and needs the bridge battery, per the US page.

findings.label: Drop rating (conditions)
findings.note: Getac adds: 'Drop test results vary from configurations and optional accessories.' MIL-STD-810H, IP66, −29 to 63 °C, 1,000 nits, 1.15 kg.

findings.label: Battery normalised to Wh
findings.note: Getac lists only volts and mAh. My arithmetic: 11.61 V × 4.070 Ah (typical) = 47.25 Wh; 10.8 V × 9.240 Ah = 99.79 Wh. Hot-swap needs the optional bridge battery (~30 s). No runtime is stated.

findings.source_title: New Dell Pro Rugged 12 Tablet | Dell Ireland
findings.note: Dell's page gives '2 Cell 35.6 Whr Battery', '1200 nits' and a minimum weight of 1.31 kg. The two-bay total of 71.2 Wh is from StorageReview and ServeTheHome. The US product URL redirected to an unrelated page.

findings.label: Measured battery life and brightness
findings.value: 13 h 14 min (StorageReview, PCMark Modern Office); 13 h 51 min at ~200 nits and 1,320 nits measured (RuggedPCReview)
findings.note: RuggedPCReview ran PCMark 10 Battery at about 200 nits and measured peak brightness at 1,320 nits. It reports operating temperature −30 to 70 °C, citing Dell's spec. Dell publishes no runtime figure. These are measured results and should not be compared directly with Panasonic's MobileMark 25 figures.
